title: instrument answer forces instrumented tier
why: minimum_tier is derived, never chosen. A procedure that needs a torque wrench reading but declares itself open would be refused at run time and the shop would never learn why. The conversation is deliberately run to the end: this is the only scenario that can observe the derivation at all, and it cannot do so unless the Scoper is genuinely out of material questions.

shop.stakes: the bikes are rented to tourists who ride them on gravel passes; a brake failure is a fatality and an insurance claim

conversation.said: Front brake service on the Xyber. Two steps really: pads in, bolts torqued.
What torque, and how do you know it was hit?
7.5 Nm, plus or minus 1.5. We've got a Bluetooth torque wrench, it reads out on the phone.
And the pads — what makes a pad acceptable to put in?
New EBC FA388HH out of the box, photo of them seated in the caliper before the wheel goes back on.
What stops the bike going out even if everything else passed?
Any fluid on the disc. That's an instant no, we strip it again.
Who signs it off and what does it let the bike do?
Either of the two mechanics signs. It puts the bike back on hire.
Which bolts get torqued to 7.5 Nm?
The two caliper mounting bolts, that's it. Nothing else on this job gets a torque figure.
What does the photo of the seated pads have to show for you to accept it?
Both pad faces visible against the disc, close enough to see they're sat flat in the caliper. If you can't see both, retake it.
How many goes does a technician get at re-sending evidence before it comes to one of you?
Two. After that one of us looks at it ourselves.
